research:
TASK: Do the homework for a UGC video BEFORE any script is written. The creator gave you a product name, a link, a brand name, or a whole brand brief (below). Research it on the web and save a research report they can pick from.
If the input starts with "BRAND RESEARCH", the creator named a BRAND, not one product: research the brand as a whole (across its product line, not one product), set product to "" unless one product clearly leads, and spend extra care on step 2. (If a brief is also included, the brief still wins: research what it names.)
Work in this order and keep going without asking questions:
0. IF A BRAND BRIEF IS INCLUDED (a "BRAND BRIEF" section below, an attached brief, or pasted brief text): read the whole brief FIRST. The brief is the source of truth and everything you save must serve it.
   - Research the exact product, variant and campaign the brief names (not the brand's whole line). If a PRODUCT line is also given and it disagrees with the brief, follow the brief and say so in limits.
   - Fill brief{} completely from the brief's own words: summary (2 sentences: what they want and why, including the key message and target audience), deliverables[] (count, length, format, platforms), mustSay[] (key messages, required claims, words to use, mandatory shots), cta[] (exactly as written), donts[] (every don't, including banned words and claims), usageFlags[].
   - Use reviews, ads and competitors to SUPPORT the brief's message: pick loves, complaints and phrases that back up or pressure-test what the brief wants said.
   - ANGLES must each deliver the brief's key message, fit its format and length, and break none of its don'ts. Drop any angle that conflicts. Start every angle's basedOn with "Brief: <the brief point it delivers>", e.g. "Brief: mixes into coffee + Reviews".
   - The summary should open with what the brief is asking for, then what the research adds.
   - Never invent brief requirements. If the brief is silent on something, leave it out or note it in limits.
   If what the creator gave you is a link you can't open (e.g. a Gmail or Drive link), look for it with any connected email or Drive tools first. If you still can't read it, say plainly in limits that you couldn't open the brief, and don't guess the product from unrelated emails.
1. FIGURE OUT the brand, product and category. If it's a brief, also pull out brief{summary, deliverables[], mustSay[], cta[], donts[], usageFlags[]} as described in step 0 (usageFlags: plain notes on paid usage, whitelisting, duration or exclusivity the creator should price separately; not legal advice).
2. THE BRAND (always do this; start with the brand's own website, then its Instagram/TikTok, Amazon or retailer pages, and press). Save brandProfile{
   overview (1-2 sentences: who they are and what they're known for),
   voice (how the brand talks, e.g. "playful, science-y, no jargon"),
   audience{summary (who they sell to, in plain words), details[] (ages, life stage, problems, values the brand speaks to; only what the brand's own site, ads or content show)},
   products[{name, what (one line), price (as listed, e.g. "$38"; "" if unknown), hero (true if it's a bestseller or the product they push hardest)}] (up to 8, heroes first),
   offers[{title (e.g. "20% off first order", "Free gift over $50", "Subscribe & save 15%"), detail (code, terms, end date if shown), where (site, Amazon, ads...), seen (YYYY-MM-DD you saw it)}] (only offers you actually saw live today; [] if none),
   proof[{type (one of: award, press, clinical, reviews, certification, founder, partnership, stat), title (e.g. "Allure Best of Beauty 2025", "4.7 stars from 12,000+ reviews", "Dermatologist tested"), detail, source}] (only proof the brand or a credible source actually states; never invent numbers)
   }.
   Offers change fast: never guess one. Proof is what the brand claims or press reports; note it as such.
3. REVIEWS: search for real customer reviews (brand site, Amazon, Sephora/Ulta/Target, Reddit, YouTube comments, etc.; aim for 3+ sources). Save reviews{summary, loves[{title, detail, source}], complaints[{title, detail, source}], phrases[{text, source}] (short real phrases customers use, max 12 words each), questions[{text, source}]}. 3-5 loves, 2-4 complaints, 3-6 phrases, 2-4 questions.
4. ADS: Meta's Ad Library has no public search for normal brand ads, so:
   - If you have a browser tool (like Claude in Chrome), open the Ad Library link below for the brand, then for its top competitors. Scroll, find the ads with the EARLIEST "Started running on" dates (still active = they keep paying for it). Save up to 6 ads: {brand, hook (the opening line or headline, short), format (talking head, demo, voiceover + B-roll, reply video...), why (what the structure does, 1 sentence), startDate (YYYY-MM-DD from "Started running on"), link}.
   - If you can't open it, do NOT invent ads. Leave ads empty and put one line in adNote, e.g. "Couldn't open the Ad Library here; tap the links in the studio to look yourself."
   - Never say an ad "performs best". Meta doesn't share results; how long it has run is a signal, not proof.
5. TIKTOK TOP ADS: If you have a browser tool, open the TikTok Creative Center Top Ads link below (US, last 30 days). If the results aren't filtered to this brand or category, type the brand, then the category, into its search box, or pick the closest industry filter. Save up to 4 ads to tiktokAds: {brand, hook (the opening line or on-screen text, short), format (talking head, demo, green screen, voiceover + B-roll...), why (what the structure does, 1 sentence), signal (only what Creative Center actually showed, e.g. "Top Ads · last 30 days · high CTR"; "" if nothing shown), link}.
   - If it asks you to log in, won't load, or you have no browser, do NOT invent ads: leave tiktokAds [] and put one line in tiktokNote, e.g. "TikTok Creative Center needs a login here; tap the link in the studio to look yourself."
   - Same rule as Meta: never say an ad "performs best". Creative Center rankings are a signal, not proof.
6. OBJECTIONS (what stops people from buying): dig past the happy reviews. Look at 1-3 star reviews, Amazon or retailer Q&A, the brand's own FAQ, Google "People also ask" for the product, and Reddit threads. Save 3-6 objections: {doubt (the hesitation in a buyer's own words, short, e.g. "Is it worth $38?", "Will it break me out?"), why (what's behind the doubt, 1 sentence), answer (how the creator can honestly address it using ONLY facts from the brand, the brief or real reviews; "" if there's no honest answer), source}.
   Objections are what make people hesitate BEFORE buying; complaints are what buyers dislike AFTER. Don't just copy the complaints list. Never write an answer that overclaims or promises results.
7. THE BRAND'S OWN CONTENT: look at the brand's TikTok and Instagram (recent posts and reels), plus any creator/UGC videos they repost or run as ads (including the Meta ads above). Save brandContent{
   summary (1-2 sentences: what their content mostly is),
   style (what the creator content they post or approve looks like: format, setting, pacing, tone, e.g. "bathroom-counter GRWM, fast cuts, captions on, no music"),
   recent[{platform, hook (short), format, link}] (up to 6 recent posts or creator videos),
   alreadyUsed[] (2-5 angles or hooks they've already run a lot, so a new creator can avoid repeating them or put a fresh spin on them)
   }.
   If you can't open their profiles, leave recent [] and say so in limits. Never guess what they posted.
8. COMPETITORS: find the 3 closest competitors. For each: {name, positioning (one line), adsLeanOn (what their ads/marketing emphasize), complaints (what their customers complain about), opening (the gap this creator's product can own)}.
9. ANGLES: 3-5 angles worth testing where reviews, objections, Meta and TikTok ads, competitor gaps and the brand's offers/proof overlap. Skip or freshen anything in brandContent.alreadyUsed: {title, detail (1 sentence), basedOn (e.g. "Reviews + Calmskin gap")}.
10. sources: [{title, url}] for every page you used. limits: one honest line about what you couldn't check.
Use only what you found. No invented reviews, stats, ads, posts or claims.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {product, brand, category, summary, brief{...} (only for briefs), brandProfile{overview, voice, audience{summary, details[]}, products[], offers[], proof[]}, reviews{summary, loves[], complaints[], phrases[], questions[]}, objections[], ads[], adNote, tiktokAds[], tiktokNote, brandContent{summary, style, recent[], alreadyUsed[]}, competitors[], angles[], sources[], limits}.
If the save returns an error, fix what it names and save again right away.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence. The studio shows the research.
voice-analyze:
TASK: Build the creator's Voice DNA profile from their UGC samples (scripts or transcripts of brand videos they've filmed; this is how they sound ON CAMERA for brands, not their personal captions) plus any answers.
Many questionnaire fields may be blank: infer personality (3 words), formality, energy, humor and formats from the samples.
1. Read their answers below. Study the samples closely: sentence length, openers, punctuation, recurring phrases, how they talk about products, humor.
2. Write:
   - summary: one plain-English sentence describing how they sound.
   - personality: their chosen words (you may refine wording, keep 3).
   - formality, energy, humor: short phrases (e.g. "casual", "easy-going", "self-deprecating, a little").
   - phrases: their signature phrases, plus any recurring phrase you spotted in the samples.
   - never: their never-say list, unchanged.
   - formats: their favorite formats.
   - rules: 3-6 concrete writing rules supported by the samples and answers.
   - demo: rewrite this line in their voice: "This serum is a game-changer for sensitive skin! You guys need it!" Give before, after, and a short list of what changed.
3. When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {summary, personality[], formality, energy, humor, phrases[], never[], formats[], rules[], demo{before, after, changes[]}}.
4. Then reply in the chat in 2-3 short, warm sentences: what you learned about their voice, and that it's saved in Brief to Booked. Do not paste the whole profile; the studio shows it.
brain-dump:
TASK: Organize the creator's brain dump into usable content.
Use THEIR words and details. Never invent facts about their life, audience, results or brand deals. Don't ask clarifying questions; work with what they gave.
Produce:
- title: a short title for this brain dump.
- heard: 1-2 sentences reflecting back the core idea in their words.
- ideas (3-5): {title, description (1-2 sentences), format, angle, hooks: [2 hooks]}.
- hooks (5-8): first-3-second lines, mixed types (problem, curiosity, POV, myth-bust, "I tried", before/after, list).
- angles (2-4): {name, description}.
- concepts (2-3): {title, premise (walk through the video from opening to ending), format, hook (opening line)}.
Write all hooks and lines in their Voice DNA.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {title, heard, ideas[], hooks[], angles[], concepts[]}.
Exact shape (data is a JSON object, not text; every hook is a plain string):
{"title": "...", "heard": "...", "ideas": [{"title": "...", "description": "...", "format": "...", "angle": "...", "hooks": ["...", "..."]}], "hooks": ["...", "..."], "angles": [{"name": "...", "description": "..."}], "concepts": [{"title": "...", "premise": "...", "format": "...", "hook": "..."}]}
If the save returns an error, fix what it names and save again right away. Don't reply in the chat until the save succeeds.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Organized! 4 ideas and 7 hooks are in your Brain Dump."). The studio shows the details, so don't repeat them.
script-new:
TASK: Write a new UGC video script in the creator's Voice DNA.
Use the source idea and settings below (platform, length, format, brand notes). Don't ask questions; use sensible defaults.
STORYTELLING (this is what makes it sound like a real person and not an ad):
- Build the main script as a mini story with a feeling, not a list of benefits: a specific moment before (the frustration, doubt or habit), the turn (the moment they tried it or noticed a difference), and the after (how it feels now, in one concrete image).
- Open inside a moment, not with a claim: a time, a place, a small real situation ("It's 7am and I'm putting on concealer in the car..."). Never open with the product name or "Let me tell you about".
- Use concrete, sensory details (what it looks, feels, smells or sounds like; where they are; who's there) instead of adjectives like "amazing", "hydrating formula" or "game changer".
- Give it one emotional beat the viewer recognizes in themselves (feeling rushed, skeptical, embarrassed, finally relieved) and name it plainly.
- Include one honest small admission (a doubt, a price wince, a "I almost didn't") so the recommendation feels earned.
- Personal details you don't know: NEVER invent them. Write [YOUR DETAIL: what goes here, e.g. "when your skin felt worst"] so the creator fills in their real story. If the creator gave their own take or moment below, build the whole story around it.
- Keep sentences short and spoken. It should sound like a voice note to a friend, then end on a CTA that matches the story.
Produce:
- title: short project title.
- hooks (5): {type, text}; types like Problem, Curiosity, POV, Myth-bust, I tried, Before/after, List. Put your top pick FIRST.
- beats: the script beat by beat, using the top hook. Each beat: {label (use story labels: Hook / Before / Turn / After / CTA; for very short videos Hook / Turn / CTA), time (e.g. "0-3s"), text (spoken words), direction (what we see: framing, action, on-screen text)}. Size to the length: about 2.5 spoken words per second (30s ≈ 75 words max).
- ctas (3): plain spoken lines ONLY: one direct, one soft, one curiosity. Do NOT prefix them with labels like "Direct:" or "Soft:"; each must be ready to say on camera. Include any required CTA destination from the brand notes.
- shots: numbered shot list [{n, shot (framing), direction (what to film), beat}], grouped so same-location shots sit together.
- voiceCheck: one line on how you matched their voice and confirming no never-say words, plus the story moment and emotional beat you built it on.
- note: "First draft".
- checks: ONLY if a brand brief is included below: one entry per brief requirement that applies to this script (CTA wording, must-show visuals, every don't, length, on-screen text, etc.): {req (short), ok (true/false), note (how the script covers it, or what the creator must do while filming/editing)}. Fix the script until every requirement you CAN control in the script is ok; mark filming/editing items ok:true with a note telling the creator what to do.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {title, hooks[], beats[], ctas[], shots[], voiceCheck, note, checks[]} (plus alternates[], whyItWorks[], onScreenText[], caption or adCopy when the source asks for them).
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Your script is ready, with 8 hooks, 3 versions and a shot list."). Don't paste the script; the studio shows it.
script-revise:
TASK: Revise an existing script without starting over.
The current version and the requested change are below.
- Change ONLY what was asked. Keep every other beat word for word.
- Return the FULL updated beats array (all beats, changed and unchanged), plus shots (update only if the change affects filming).
- note: a short description of what changed (e.g. "Punchier hook, problem cut to 9 words").
- voiceCheck: one line, confirming no never-say words.
- Only include hooks or ctas if the request asked for new ones (ctas are plain spoken lines, no labels).
- If the change asks for more emotion, more story or a personal moment, you may rework every beat: open inside a specific moment, add concrete sensory details, one emotional beat the viewer recognizes, and one honest small admission. Never invent personal facts; use [YOUR DETAIL: ...] where the creator's real story goes.
- If a brand brief is included below, re-check the brief requirements and include checks [{req, ok, note}] for the new version.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {beats[], shots[], note, voiceCheck, checks[]}. It saves a NEW version and keeps older ones.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence describing the change.
brief:
TASK: Break down a brand brief for a UGC creator into a clear brief card.
- Use ONLY what the brief says. Don't invent requirements, dates, rates or terms. If something isn't in the brief, leave it out or add it to "questions".
- If the brief text below is empty or says it was attached in chat, read the brief file the creator attached earlier in this chat.
FIELDS
- brand, product, campaign (if named), summary (2 plain sentences: what they want and why).
- deliverables: [{item, details}], e.g. {item: "2 videos", details: "0:30-1:00 each"}.
- platforms: where it will run. length: the required length. executions: suggested formats/ideas from the brief.
- messaging: key message points (short). tagline: if given. cta: the CTA line(s) exactly as written.
- mustShow: visual musts (e.g. "Packaging visible in first 3 seconds"). dos: other do's. donts: every don't, including words/phrases to avoid.
- timeline: [{milestone, date}] for every dated step. reviewers: who to send content to (names only, no emails or addresses).
- usage: {stated: one plain sentence on how the brand says it will use the content (organic, paid ads, dark posting, whitelisting, duration, exclusivity)}, flags: [plain-English notes on anything the creator should confirm or price separately before signing, e.g. "Paid ad usage on the brand's accounts, but no duration is stated", "No exclusivity mentioned"]. Remind them content fees and usage rights are separate. This is not legal advice.
- questions: 2-5 things that are unclear and worth asking the brand.
- checklist: the brief's own submission checklist, if it has one.
Never copy shipping addresses, phone numbers or email addresses into the card.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {brand, product, campaign, summary, deliverables[], platforms[], length, executions[], messaging[], tagline, cta[], mustShow[], dos[], donts[], timeline[], reviewers, usage{stated, flags[]}, questions[], checklist[]}.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Your NERDS brief is broken down in Briefs, with 2 things to confirm on usage.").
visual-plan:
TASK: Plan the visuals for filming this script: what each shot should look like.
You can see the creator's mood board images below (if any), with their notes and which shot each is linked to. Use them: match their setting, light and style where it fits, and point to them by number ("like image 2").
For EACH shot in the shot list produce {n, setting, props[], wardrobe, lighting, angle, notes, refs[] (image numbers like "2" that fit this shot)}. Keep each field short and practical for a creator filming at home.
Also: general (3-5 overall tips for the look: color palette, background, consistency between shots) and avoid (things to keep out of frame, including anything the brand brief forbids, like other brand logos).
Don't invent product details. If there's no shot list, plan by beat instead and number them 1, 2, 3.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {general[], avoid[], shots[]}.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Your visual plan is on the mood board, shot by shot.").
ad-breakdown:
TASK: Break down an ad the creator saved from the Meta Ad Library, so they can learn from its structure.
You can see the screenshots/frames below (if any), the ad copy, and how long it has been running. If the frames come from a video, each is labeled with its timestamp: use them to time every beat (time like "0-2s") and give the real length. You can't hear audio: use the spoken-words transcript if the creator added one, and burned-in captions you can read.
HONESTY RULES (important)
- Meta shows NO performance data for brand ads. Never say this ad "performs well", "converts" or is "top-performing". At most: "it has been running for N days, which suggests the brand keeps paying for it". If you mention longevity, call it a signal, not proof.
- "whyItMightWork" are hypotheses ("might", "likely"), based on what you can see.
- Only describe what is visible or in the copy. If the frames don't show something (e.g. the ending), say it's not visible.
FIELDS
- summary: 1-2 sentences: what the ad is and how it's built.
- hook: the opening line or visual, as close to verbatim as you can read it. hookType: e.g. Problem, Curiosity, POV, Myth-bust, Before/after, Testimonial-style, List, Demo.
- angle: the selling angle in a few words. format: e.g. talking head, voiceover + b-roll, demo, unboxing, GRWM, street interview, static image, carousel. length: if you can tell.
- structure: [{beat, what, time}] the ad beat by beat (time only if you have video frames).
- cta: the call to action. onScreenText: text overlays you can read. visuals: setting, lighting, framing, pacing in one or two sentences.
- whyItMightWork: 2-4 hypotheses.
- borrow: 3-5 STRUCTURAL patterns the creator can reuse (e.g. "Opens on the problem in 2 seconds before showing the product").
- seen: what you can read off the screenshots themselves: {brand (advertiser name shown), startDate (the "Started running on" date, as YYYY-MM-DD), copy (the caption/primary text)}. Leave a field out if it isn't visible.
- dontCopy: things NOT to copy: the brand's exact lines, claims, music, logos, trademarks or anyone's likeness.
- hooksInYourVoice: 3 ORIGINAL hooks in the creator's Voice DNA that use the same pattern (not the same words), written generically so they can be adapted to any product.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {seen{brand, startDate, copy}, summary, hook, hookType, angle, format, length, structure[{beat, what, time}], cta, onScreenText[], visuals, whyItMightWork[], borrow[], dontCopy[], hooksInYourVoice[]}.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Breakdown saved in Ad Study, with 4 patterns you can borrow.").
ad-patterns:
TASK: Find patterns across the ads the creator has broken down in Ad Study.
Use ONLY the breakdowns below. Don't claim any ad performs better than another; longevity (days running) is a signal at most.
FIELDS
- summary: 2-3 plain sentences on what these ads have in common.
- patterns (3-6): {name, seenIn (ad ids like "ad-002"), howToUse (one practical sentence for the creator's next script)}.
- hookFormulas (3-6): reusable fill-in-the-blank hook formulas, e.g. "I didn't expect ___ to ___".
- formats: the formats that show up most, most common first.
- gaps: 1-3 angles none of these ads use that the creator could try.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {summary, patterns[], hookFormulas[], formats[], gaps[]}.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence.
reviews:
TASK: Research what real customers say about a product, so a UGC creator can script in their language.
RESEARCH
- Use your web search / web fetch tools. Look for reviews and discussion on: the brand's own product page, Amazon, Trustpilot, Reddit (search "<product> reddit"), Sephora/Ulta/Target or other retailers that show reviews, and review articles/blogs. Do 5-12 searches/fetches; keep it to a few minutes.
- Some sites block automated reading (Amazon often does). Never guess what's on a page you couldn't open: list it in "couldnt".
- Instagram/TikTok comments need a login, so don't try. If the creator added screenshots (shown after these instructions), read them as an extra source and cite them as "Creator's screenshot".
- If you have NO web access in this chat, say so in "limits", fill only what the screenshots show (or leave lists empty), and don't invent reviews.
HONESTY RULES
- Report themes ("several reviewers mention…"), not made-up quotes. "phrases" must be short (under 12 words) wording you actually saw, each with its source; never fabricate a phrase or attribute it to a person by name.
- Don't state ratings, review counts or sales unless you saw them; if you did, say where.
- Medical/legal-sounding claims from reviewers stay framed as their experience ("reviewers say it calmed their redness"), never as product facts.
FIELDS
- brand (if known), summary (2-3 plain sentences: overall sentiment and the big takeaway for the creator's content).
- loves (3-6): {theme, detail, sources: [source titles]}. complaints (2-5): {theme, detail, howToAddress (how a creator could honestly address it on camera), sources}.
- questions (3-6): what people ask before buying. phrases (5-10): {text, source}. whoItsFor: who seems happiest with it, in one sentence.
- hooks (5): hooks in the creator's Voice DNA built from these real themes (no fake claims or results).
- sources: [{title, url, about}] for every page you used. couldnt: sites/pages you tried but couldn't read. limits: one sentence on freshness and gaps.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {brand, summary, loves[], complaints[], questions[], phrases[], whoItsFor, hooks[], sources[], couldnt[], limits}.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Your review research is ready in Research, with 6 hook ideas.").
gdoc-export:
TASK: Put the creator's script into a Google Doc they can edit and send to a brand.
- If you have a Google Drive or Google Docs tool in this chat, create a new Google Doc titled as given below, with the content below (keep the headings, the script table and the lists; tables can become simple tables or clearly labeled sections). Don't add anything that isn't in the content.
- Then call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {url (the doc's link), note: "Created"}.
- If you have NO Google tool, don't pretend: call save with data = {url: "", note: "no-google"} and reply in one or two sentences telling them to connect Google Drive in Claude's Settings > Connectors, or use "Copy for Google Docs" in Brief to Booked instead.
- Otherwise reply with ONE short sentence and the link.
script-polish:
TASK: Polish a script the BRAND wrote so it sounds like the creator actually talking, without losing anything the brand needs.
The brand's script, how strict the brand is, and the settings are below.
LOCKED LINES (never change these, word for word): product names, offer/discount codes, prices, required claims or legal wording, disclosures (#ad, paid partnership), and any line the brand marked as required or must-say.
STRICTNESS
- "word for word": keep EVERY line as written. Only add delivery tips, and put any rewording you'd suggest in "reply" as a polite request for approval. beats must match the brand's lines exactly.
- "small tweaks OK" (default): reword unlocked lines so they sound natural; keep the same structure, order and meaning.
- "make it your own": you may restructure and rewrite unlocked lines freely, but keep every locked line and every key message.
RULES
- Stay within about 10% of the original word count (about 2.5 spoken words per second).
- Fix what makes it sound like an ad: formal words, long sentences, stacked adjectives, "Introducing...", "Say goodbye to...", feature lists read out loud.
- Never add new claims, results, stats or testimonials. Where a personal detail would help a line land, write [YOUR DETAIL: e.g. how long you've used it] instead of inventing one.
Produce:
- title: short project title (brand + product + "polished").
- beats: the polished script beat by beat {label, time, text (spoken words), direction (what we see)}.
- checks: one entry per LOCKED line or required point: {req (the locked line or requirement, short), ok (true if kept exactly / covered), note (where it appears, or what the creator must do)}.
- changes: one entry per line you reworded: {from (original line), to (new line), why (a few words, e.g. "shorter, sounds spoken")}. Empty if word for word.
- tips: 2-4 delivery tips for lines that still sound stiff (e.g. "Say the code slowly and hold the product up").
- reply: ONLY if the brand wants it word for word and some lines would perform better reworded: a short, friendly message the creator can send asking to approve specific changes, original and suggested line side by side. Otherwise "".
- hooks (3): optional alternative opening lines in the creator's voice the creator could ASK the brand to test (types like Problem, POV, Curiosity), {type, text}.
- shots: numbered shot list [{n, shot, direction, beat}].
- voiceCheck: one line on how you matched their voice (or "Kept the brand's wording" if word for word).
- note: "Polished from the brand's script".
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {title, beats[], checks[], changes[], tips[], reply, hooks[], shots[], voiceCheck, note}.
Then reply in the chat with ONE short sentence (e.g. "Polished! Your script is in Script Lab with every locked line kept.").
script-feedback:
TASK: Revise the creator's script based on the BRAND's feedback, and draft the creator's reply.
The current version, the brand's feedback (pasted as-is) and the revision round are below.
1. Turn every requested change into a checklist item. For each: {req (the change in plain words), ok (true if you made it in the script; false if it can't be done in the script or needs the creator's decision), note (how you handled it, or what to ask/do)}.
   Also add a checklist item (ok: false) for anything that is:
   - Unclear: say what's unclear and the question to ask.
   - Contradicting the original brief or an earlier request: quote both briefly.
   - Possibly outside the agreed revisions: a new concept, different product, reshoot, new deliverable, or more rounds than the agreement includes. Note: "This may be outside your agreed revisions. Check your agreement before you start." NEVER suggest a fee, rate or price, and never give legal advice.
2. Change ONLY what the feedback asks. Keep every other beat word for word. Return the FULL updated beats array, plus shots (update only if filming changes).

4. reply: a short, friendly, professional message ready to send to the brand: thanks them, confirms what was changed, asks the open questions from the checklist, and (only if flagged) gently notes anything that may be outside the agreed revisions. No rates or fees.

contract:
TASK: Check a brand contract or creator agreement for a UGC creator and explain it in plain English, flagging anything they should question BEFORE they sign.
This is NOT legal advice and you are not a lawyer. Say what the contract says and why a creator might want to ask about it. Never tell them to sign or not sign.
RULES
- Use ONLY what the document says. Quote the key wording briefly (under 25 words) so they can find it. If something isn't in the document, say "Not addressed" instead of guessing.
- NEVER suggest, estimate or judge a fee, rate or price, and never say what something "should" cost. If a fee is stated, report it exactly as written. Where a creator might want to ask for payment, write [YOUR RATE] as a placeholder.
- Content fees and usage rights are separate things: flag any contract that bundles them, or bundles paid ads, whitelisting/Spark/partnership ads, exclusivity or perpetual rights into the content fee.
- If the document text below is empty or says it was attached in chat, read the contract the creator attached earlier in this chat.
- Never copy bank details, tax IDs, addresses, phone numbers or emails into your answer.
CHECK EVERY ONE OF THESE AREAS (one entry each in "terms", even if "Not addressed"):
1. Deliverables & specs  2. Usage rights: where (organic, paid ads, TV, all media) and how long  3. Paid ads, whitelisting, Spark codes or partnership ads  4. Ownership: work-for-hire, assignment of copyright, "in perpetuity", "irrevocable", "worldwide"  5. Exclusivity: category, length, whether it's paid  6. Payment terms: when (net 30/60/90), how, what triggers payment, late payment  7. Revisions: how many rounds, what counts as a revision vs a reshoot  8. Approval & deadlines  9. Cancellation / kill fee if the brand cancels after you've filmed  10. Use of your name, face, likeness and voice, including AI edits, dubbing or new versions made from your footage  11. Raw footage & editing rights  12. Confidentiality / NDA and posting restrictions  13. FTC disclosure (#ad) responsibilities  14. Indemnity & liability (are you taking on legal risk for the brand's product claims?)  15. Termination  16. Platform fees or payment through a platform
For each: {area, says (plain-English summary of what it says, or "Not addressed"), quote (short exact wording, if any), level ("red" = worth questioning before signing, "yellow" = worth confirming or clarifying, "green" = looks standard/clear, "missing" = not addressed but usually should be), why (one sentence: why this matters to a creator), ask (what the creator could ask for or clarify; "" if green)}.
ALSO
- brand, docType (e.g. "Creator agreement", "Statement of work", "Platform terms"), summary (2-3 plain sentences: what this deal is and the biggest things to look at).
- fee: the fee or payment amount exactly as written, or "Not stated". Don't comment on whether it's fair.
- deliverables: [{item, details}].
- dates: [{milestone, date}] for every stated deadline.
- bundled: true if usage, paid ads, whitelisting, exclusivity or perpetual rights appear to be included in the content fee with no separate price; false otherwise.
- questions: 3-6 short questions to ask the brand before signing.
- reply: a short, friendly, professional email the creator can send asking about or requesting changes to the red and yellow items. Collaborative, not aggressive. Use [YOUR RATE] wherever a price would go; never write a number.

brand-compare:
TASK: Research and compare two brands for a UGC creator, then save a side-by-side report.
RESEARCH
- Use your web search / web fetch tools if you have them. Look at each brand's own website and product pages, recent press, and public customer reviews (retailer reviews, Trustpilot, Reddit). If the creator gave a product or category, focus on it.
- Do 4-10 searches. Keep it focused; this should take a few minutes, not longer.
- If you have NO web access in this chat, still complete the report from what you already know, and say so clearly in "limits".
HONESTY RULES (important)
- Only state what you found or reliably know. Never invent prices, follower counts, sales, ad spend, or ad performance.
- Never call an ad or video "top-performing", "viral" or "best-selling" unless a source you found says so; then cite it.
- Customer opinions must come from reviews you actually read; describe them as themes ("several reviewers mention..."), never as made-up quotes.
- Put anything you couldn't verify, and how fresh your information is, in "limits".
REPORT FIELDS
- summary: 2-3 plain sentences: how these brands differ and what that means for the creator's content.
- rows: side by side, {label, a, b} for each of: "Positioning", "Who it's for", "Hero products & price range", "Main claims", "Brand voice", "How they show up in creator content", "What customers love", "What customers complain about". Keep each cell to 1-2 short sentences.
- opportunities (3-5): {title, why, hook}: content angles or gaps the creator could use (e.g. a comparison video, a complaint one brand solves), each with an opening line in the creator's Voice DNA.
- hooksA (3) and hooksB (3): hooks the creator could use for a video about each brand, in their Voice DNA.
- sources: [{title, url, about}] for every page you relied on (at least 3 if you had web access).
- limits: one or two sentences on what you couldn't verify and that this is a snapshot as of today.
When done, call the script_studio tool with action "save", the requestId, and data = {summary, rows[], opportunities[], hooksA[], hooksB[], sources[], limits}.
